title: Uniform semiclassical phase mixing and scattering for the linearized Hartree equation under uniform Penrose stability
source_title: Phase mixing for the Hartree equation and Landau damping in the semiclassical limit
author: Marnie Smith
difficulty_reason: The assumed Penrose lower bound alone does not provide density decay or a scattering profile uniform as hbar tends to zero. The author supplies the full quantum Lindhard derivative and Green-function inversion estimates, then uses the source-specific free-density convolution to control the interacting density. The complete finite-difference, weighted Fourier-variable and tail-integral argument closes the moving quantum Sobolev scattering estimate with uniform constants, rather than treating that new semiclassical estimate as a standard prerequisite.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Proposition2.11 in integer-regularity range: d>=3, M=ceil((d+1)/2), nonnegative integers N0,N1 with N1<N0-d/2-1, real short-range w in L1(Rd), steady distribution g of weighted Sobolev regularity H_(2+ceil(d/2))^(N0+9/2+delta0), and exact uniform Penrose condition2. Initial Qin has finite quantum H_(M,M)^(N0+1) norm. The linearized Hartree solution22 has Fourier density bounded by C norm(Qin)/<k,kt>^N0 and scatters to Qinf in quantum H^N1 with the exact <t grad_x,grad_xi>^N1 error bounded by C norm(Qin)/<t>^(d/2), uniformly hbar in(0,1]. No nonlinear bootstrap, Coulomb interaction or independently proved quantum-to-classical scattering limit claimed. Full new Lindhard derivative/resolvent and Green core33–35, free-density convolution and finite-difference scattering36–37 read; Fourier/Volterra derivation26–27 and quantum norms/Wigner free estimate7–14 read. Trace Lemma2.2 is explicitly published Bedrossian–Masmoudi–Mouhot reference3; elementary moment commutation, Fourier/Laplace contour deformation and FaadiBruno are stated background with authored estimates. Integer N0,N1 retained so the printed integer inverse-Laplace derivative count applies directly; no fractional regularity extrapolation supplied. Entire65-page original context retained, JEP13(2026) DOI10.5802/jep.353 and exact author/license checked.
